title: Anna Livia Plurabelle
speakers_note: Joyce rarely marks who speaks. This split follows the call-and-answer rhythm of the dialogue and is one reading among several.

items.text: O tell me all about Anna Livia! I want to hear all about Anna Livia.
items.note: The chapter opens with one washerwoman begging the other for gossip. On the page these words form a triangle, the delta: Joyce's sign for ALP and the shape of a river mouth.
items.speaker: a

items.text: every telling has a taling and that's the he and the she of it.
items.note: Telling, tale and tail at once. Every story has a sequel and two sides, his and hers, which is the whole method of the book.
items.speaker: b

items.text: Anna was, Livia is, Plurabelle's to be.
items.note: Past, present and future in seven words: Vico's cycle again. It also echoes the prayer line about what was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be.
items.speaker: a

items.text: A tale told of Shaun or Shem?
items.note: Dusk is falling and the gossip turns to the twins. The women can no longer agree on which son is which.
items.speaker: b

items.text: Can't hear with the waters of.
items.note: The river grows louder as night comes, and the sentence breaks off the way the women lose each other's words across the water.
items.speaker: a

items.text: My foos won't moos. I feel as old as yonder elm.
items.speak: My foos won't moos. I feel as old as yonder elm.
items.note: Her feet won't move. One washerwoman is turning into the elm on the bank; the other is becoming a stone.
items.speaker: b

items.speak: Tell me tale of stem or stone.
items.note: Tell me a tale, run together. Stem and stone are the tree and the rock the women become, and also the twins: Shem and Shaun, the living and the fixed.
items.speaker: a

items.text: Beside the rivering waters of, hitherandthithering waters of. Night!
items.speak: Beside the rivering waters of, hither and thithering waters of. Night!
items.note: The chapter's last words. Joyce chose this ending for his own 1929 recording, and it is the best place to hear the Wake as music.
items.speaker: b
